subsystems.name: Ground-based millimetre and submillimetre spectroscopy
subsystems.role: measures trace gases in the cloud deck from Earth through narrow atmospheric windows.
parts: single-dish telescopes at high dry sites

subsystems.name: Orbital remote sensing
subsystems.role: maps cloud composition and vertical structure from Venus orbit.

subsystems.name: Radiative transfer and retrieval software
subsystems.role: turns raw spectra into gas abundances with honest error bars.

subsystems.name: Laboratory reference spectroscopy
subsystems.role: supplies the absorption line data the retrievals depend on.

subsystems.name: Photochemical modelling
subsystems.role: tests whether known chemistry can explain the observed abundances.

subsystems.name: In-situ verification (planned)
subsystems.role: would settle the question by sampling the clouds directly.
parts: mass spectrometer on a descent probe

buildSteps.title: Choose a spectral window
buildSteps.detail: Find a narrow wavelength band where Venus's own atmosphere is transparent enough for a trace gas line to reach a telescope.

buildSteps.title: Observe and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Record the spectrum alongside a reference source, and correct for Earth's atmosphere and the telescope's own response.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve the abundance
buildSteps.detail: Fit a radiative transfer model to the line depth to estimate how many molecules per billion are present, and how uncertain that is.

buildSteps.title: Compare with known chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Run a photochemical model to see whether volcanoes, lightning, surface minerals or sunlight-driven reactions could make the same amount.

buildSteps.title: Test the claim against other instruments
buildSteps.detail: Re-observe with a different telescope, wavelength and calibration path; a real signal must survive all of them.

buildSteps.title: Check for confusion
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the line is not a different molecule — sulfur dioxide shares nearby wavelengths — and not an artefact of data processing.

buildSteps.title: Probe habitability separately
buildSteps.detail: Model whether cloud droplets of concentrated sulfuric acid could support any biochemistry at all, given that it destroys organic molecules.

buildSteps.title: Send a probe
buildSteps.detail: A future descent craft would ingest cloud particles and measure their chemistry directly, ending the remote-sensing argument.

prerequisites.why: the key phosphorus and sulfur lines fall at wavelengths only large radio observatories can resolve.
abundance estimates are only as good as the reference line strengths used to fit them.
the sulfur cycle is reasonably modelled; the phosphorus cycle is far less certain.
whether concentrated sulfuric acid can host any stable biochemistry is unresolved.
no mission has yet measured the cloud particles' composition directly.

pathway.milestone: continued ground-based monitoring with independent instruments and open data
pathway.unlocks: settling whether the disputed phosphine line is real, sulfur dioxide, or noise.

pathway.milestone: dedicated Venus orbiters with modern ultraviolet and infrared spectrometers
pathway.unlocks: global, time-resolved maps of sulfur and phosphorus species.

pathway.milestone: a descent probe through the cloud deck
pathway.unlocks: direct measurement of droplet chemistry and any non-equilibrium gases.

pathway.milestone: a cloud-level sampling platform or sample return
